100,000 Aeons Ago: The Aspiration wealthy householder in Harnsavatt offered seven-day feast to Buddha Padumuttara. He made single wish: to become the foremost monk with sweet voice in future Buddha’s dispensation. the Buddha confirmed his elles se

Life as Cittapatta Cuckoo 0 During the time of Buddha Vipassi the future Bhaddiya lived as cuckoo bird. Seeing the Buddha, he joyfully altered his flight and dropped single ripe mango into the alms bowl

The Seed of Sweet Voice Overjoyed by his offering, the cuckoo spent week reflecting on the Buddha’s attributes without eating. This pure, sustained mental joy was specific karmic catalyst guaranteeing his exquisitely sweet voice in future lives.

The Shrinking Shrine After Buddha Kassapa’s Parinibbana, devotees debated relic shrine’s size. The master carpenter intervened, drastically reducing the proposed seven-league shrine down to one league to ensure it could be easily repaired in the future.

The Law of Karmic Consequence The cosmic law of karma is mathematically precise. Because the carpenter deliberately reduced the physical size of the supreme Buddha’s shrine, he was reborn with dwarfish, extremely short body in all subsequent existences.

The Final Existence in Savatthi Reborn as Bhaddiya, his outward stature was small, but his faith was immense. He ordained under Buddha Gotama, receiving direct meditation instructions to nurture stout, undefiled heart.

The Dried River of Craving Guided by Ven. Sariputta, Bhaddiya attained full Awakening (Arahatship). The morally defiling river of craving that binds beings to Sarnsara was permanently dried up by the sun of the Arahat path.

The Illusion of Appearance Outwardly, worldly monks mocked Bhaddiya's dwarfish frame. Inwardly, his mind was untouched. To protect his mockers from karma, the compassionate Bhaddiya walked silently behind them, entirely free from the fetters of anger.
The Anatomy of Flawless Chariot Buddha Gotama revealed Bhaddiya’s inner perfection through the of chariot:
Wheel: Flawless Morality
Spokes: Incomparable Mindfulness
